(C.I.D.) Office Notes
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
File No. C. I. D. REGISTER
No. I. O. D. 1196.
Date 25 . 4 . - 30.

It would appear that Mr Blunt
is taking up this matter but
as the incidents occurred on
Municipal Road. I suggest
that it should be brought
to the notice of the Council
by the Police so that an
official protest can be lodged
with the Senior Consul.

The molestation was not
serious but it shows an
anti-foreign attitude which
may develop if these soldiers are
not warned officially.

I will also get in touch
with the proper military authorities
if you wish & ask them
to take up the matter.

S. C. Myers
D.C. (Crs. B.)

gladful
2/4

(b) I do not think
it is necessary.
You need not do anything
except keep a watch.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
档案号：C. I. D. 登记册
I. O. D. 1196 号。
日期 30年4月25日。

看来 Blunt 先生正在处理此事，但
鉴于事件发生在
工部局道路上，我建议
由警方将此事项提请
工部局注意，以便向
首席领事提出正式抗议。

骚扰行为并不
严重，但这显示了一种
排外态度，如果不对这些士兵
进行正式警告，这种态度可能会
进一步发展。

如果您愿意，我也将联系
相应的军事当局，并请他们
处理此事。

S. C. Myers
副督察长（巡捕房 B 区）

page_data.en:
Special Branch
(Foreign Section)
(C.I.D.) Office Notes
File No. 10 D 1196
April 22, 1930.

Sir,

With reference to attached newspaper article,
I interviewed Mrs. Biggs, British, teacher in the Girls
School Yu Yuen Road and residing at No. 268A Yu Yuen Road.
Mrs. Biggs informed me that on Sunday, April 6th, she
had a visit from a friend, Miss J. Carnaghan, Senior
Supervisor in the Shanghai Mutual Telephone Coy and
residing at No. 29 Macgregor Road.

After tiffin the two ladies decided to go for a
walk and set out in the Keswick Road direction. About
3 p.m. they were passing along that road when they
encountered about 20 Chinese soldiers. Some were swinging
their belts and laughing and passing rude remarks about
foreign women. On passing there Mrs. Biggs received a
slight tip from a belt. The blow did not hurt but the
soldiers seemed to think it great fun. Several stones
were also thrown after them but fortunately they were not
struck.

A little while later Mrs. Biggs and Miss Carnaghan
passed another group of soldiers on Lincoln Avenue near
the junction of the new Chinese road. They were there
again subjected to abusive language and several stones
thrown but neither were struck.

Nothing further happened on the way home.
Mr. Blunt, H.B.M. Consul has interviewed Mrs. Biggs
on the subject.

Dhouneay
D. S. I.

D. C.
(C. & S. Branches)

（批：D.C. (C. & S. Branches), This incident seems to have been of a very minor nature. JRL 24/4）

特别分部
（外籍科）
（刑事侦缉处）办公笔记
档案号 10 D 1196
1930年4月22日。

先生，

关于所附报纸文章，
我约谈了 Biggs 夫人，英国人，系愚园路女子学校教师，
居住于愚园路 268A 号。
Biggs 夫人告知我，4月6日星期日，
她的一位朋友 J. Carnaghan 小姐来访，Carnaghan 小姐是上海电话公司的高级督导员，
居住于麦格罗路 29 号。

午餐后，两位女士决定去散步，并朝
开思威克路方向出发。下午3点左右，她们沿该路行走时，
遇到了约20名中国士兵。其中一些人甩着腰带，大笑，
并对外国妇女发表粗鲁言论。经过那里时，Biggs 夫人
被腰带轻微碰了一下。这一击并未造成伤害，但士兵们
似乎觉得这很有趣。随后还向她们扔了几块石头，但幸运的是
未被击中。

过了一会儿，Biggs 夫人和 Carnaghan 小姐
在林肯大道靠近新华路交界处附近，又经过另一群士兵。她们在那里
再次遭到辱骂，并被投掷数块石头，但均未击中。

回家途中未再发生其他事情。
英国驻华总领事 Blunt 先生已就此事约谈了 Biggs 夫人。

Dhouneay
高级警探

副督察长
（刑事及特别分部）

（批注：副督察长（刑事及特别分部），此事件性质似乎非常轻微。JRL 4月24日）

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, APRIL 9, 1930

THE DANGER OF THE
OUTSIDE ROADS

Better to Keep off Them Because
of the Unruly soldiery:
Unpleasant Incidents

A short time ago a warning was
issued to the citizens of the Inter-
national Settlement to stay out of
Chinese territory after dark so that
they would not be annoyed by rob-
bers or possible kidnappers. It ap-
pears, from recent complaints, that
foreign citizens will not only have
to stay in their own territory after
dark but also during the day and
that they may not even travel on
extra-settlement municipal roads.
Chinese soldiers are forbidden to go
armed along the Municipal Roads
but there is nothing to prevent them
from going across the boundaries
for personal business or pleasure
when they are not on duty. They
are particularly numerous along the
Soochow creek roads, strolling about
in groups of ten or twelve. And
foreigners who stroll too near the
Red Joss House on Keswick Road,
or the new Chinese road near Lin-
coln Avenue are very apt to be sub-
ject to the insolence and insults of
the Chinese soldiers. The Municipal
Police Force is trying to control
these soldiers while they are on duty
and to keep them off of foreign
roads but the casual passer-by is
often an object for their stone-
throwing and intimidating.

Two Ladies Struck

Late yesterday two English ladies
were walking on Keswick Road, on
the settlement side of the railroad
tracks. They were intercepted by a
band of Chinese soldiers who were
strolling along the road although they
were not on duty. One of them had
a rifle slung over his shoulder and as the
ladies passed he jostled one of them who
was struck with a blow. The soldiers
laughed at the incident and then strolled
on. This is one of the many cases
where foreigners are subjected to insult
and even violence by Chinese soldiers
who are supposed to be under control.
It is high time that something was done
to stop this sort of thing. The Municipal
Council should take steps to prevent
such occurrences. It is not enough to
issue warnings to citizens to stay off
the roads. The soldiers themselves
should be punished for their actions.
The Municipal Police should be given
more power to deal with these cases.
It is a disgrace to the city that such
things should happen.

At the intersection of the new
Chinese road with the Lincoln
Avenue the two women passed a
group of soldiers on the Chinese
side of the road. Although the two
were on foreign road the Chinese,
who were on guard, threw mud and
sticks at them from their own side.
It has been no uncommon pro-
cedure during the last two or three
years for the Chinese police to be
on patrol on the outlying Municipal
roads. No official announcement has
been made to the effect that the
Council is taking steps to prevent
Chinese patrol on Municipal roads
or Chinese soldiery over the bound-
aries on the Settlement side. When
the Chinese police first began this
patrolling they were limited to the
area along Brennan piece. Later
on they went to Hungjao and
Rubicon roads. Evidently the police
do not believe it worth while to
patrol Monument Road or Pearce
Road which are still further beyond
the Rubicon. Six or seven police
officer's headquarters have been built
along some of the outlying Muni-
cipal roads. They have even taken
posts in the general vicinity of
Jessfield Road. Last Sunday there
were four armed soldiers with rifles
and bandoliers walking up and down
Pearce Road.

Several weeks ago a foreign
Omnibus Co. inspector became en-
tangled in an argument with several
Chinese police over the matter of
proper fare. Although the police
were formidable the inspector escap-
ed without injury due to the fact
that the Chinese passengers in the
bus took the side of the inspector.
Shanghai residents will remember
the murder of Mr. Mackenzie on
Keswick Road several years ago,
and still more recently the attempt-
ed murder of Miss Duncan on the
same road. Miss Thompson was
murdered and Mr. Law was wound-
ed near the Red Joss House less
than two years ago.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，1930年4月9日，星期三

界外道路的危险

因军纪涣散的士兵，最好远离这些道路：
不愉快的事件

不久前，曾向国际租界市民发出警告，要求他们在天黑后不要进入中国地界，以免受到强盗或可能的绑匪的骚扰。根据最近的投诉来看，外国公民不仅要在天黑后待在自己的地界内，白天也是如此，甚至可能不得在越界筑路的工部局道路上通行。中国士兵被禁止携带武器沿工部局道路行进，但在非执勤期间，没有什么能阻止他们越过边界办理私事或娱乐。他们在苏州河沿岸道路上尤其众多，常以十人或十二人为一组四处游荡。而在开思威克路上靠近红庙，或林肯大道附近的新华路漫步的外国人，很容易遭受中国士兵的无礼和侮辱。工部局警务处正试图控制执勤期间的这些士兵，并让他们远离外国人的道路，但偶然的过路人经常成为他们投掷石块和恐吓的对象。

两名女士遭袭

昨天傍晚，两名英国女士走在铁轨租界一侧的开思威克路上。她们被一群在路上闲逛的中国士兵拦住，尽管这些士兵当时并未执勤。其中一人肩上斜挎着一支步枪，当女士们经过时，他推搡了其中一人，导致其受到一击。士兵们对此事哈哈大笑，然后继续闲逛。这是外国人遭受本应受控的中国士兵侮辱甚至暴力的众多案例之一。是时候采取某些措施来制止此类行为了。工部局应采取措施防止此类事件发生。仅向市民发出远离道路的警告是不够的。应对士兵的行为进行惩罚。应赋予工部局警务处更多权力来处理此类案件。发生此类事情是城市的耻辱。

在新华路与林肯大道的交叉口，这两名妇女经过了路中方一侧的一群士兵。虽然两人都在外国道路上，但负责警戒的中国人从自己的一侧向她们投掷泥土和棍棒。在过去两三年里，中国警察在偏远的工部局道路上巡逻已并非罕见程序。官方尚未发布公告表明工部局正采取措施防止中国警察在工部局道路上巡逻，或防止中国军人越过边界进入租界一侧。当中国警察刚开始这种巡逻时，他们仅限于勃伦南地块沿线区域。后来他们去了虹桥路和卢比孔路。显然，警方认为不值得在更远离卢比孔路的纪念碑路或皮尔斯路进行巡逻。在一些偏远的工部局道路沿线已建立了六七个警察分局。他们甚至在极司菲尔路附近的一般区域设立了岗位。上个星期日，有四名携带步枪和子弹带的武装士兵在皮尔斯路上来回走动。

几周前，一家外国公共汽车公司的稽查员因车费问题与几名中国警察陷入争执。尽管警察气势汹汹，但由于车上的中国乘客站在稽查员一边，稽查员得以未受伤害而脱身。上海居民会记得几年前发生在开思威克路上的麦肯齐先生谋杀案，以及更近期发生在同一条路上的邓肯小姐未遂谋杀案。不到两年前，汤普森小姐被谋杀，劳先生则在红庙附近受伤。
